aboutGame.title: What is Rivetina archibaldi?
paragraphs: Rivetina archibaldi is a praying mantis in the order Mantodea and family Rivetinidae, formally described as a species new to science in 2026. It was named from material collected in the Zagros oak forests of western Iran.

The species is a compact, ground-associated mantis with raptorial forelegs, a mobile triangular head, and mottled earth-tone coloration. Its published description provides the taxonomy, morphology, type locality, and a male-based identification key for Iranian Rivetina species.

faq.title: Rivetina archibaldi FAQ
faq.description: Quick answers to common questions about the Rivetina archibaldi species, its habitat, identification, and scientific record.

items.question: What is Rivetina archibaldi?
items.answer: Rivetina archibaldi is a praying mantis in the family Rivetinidae, formally described in 2026 from the Zagros oak forests of western Iran.

items.question: Where does Rivetina archibaldi live?
items.answer: The published type locality is in the Zagros oak forest belt of western Iran. Surveys focus on the ground layer, low vegetation, bark, and leaf litter.

items.question: How do I identify Rivetina archibaldi?
items.answer: Document the overall build, pronotum profile, foreleg spination, wing length, and head shape. The published identification key is male-based, so expert review is important for species-level confirmation.

items.question: When was Rivetina archibaldi described?
items.answer: The species was described in 2026 in the Journal of Orthoptera Research, volume 35, issue 2, pages 283–292.

items.question: What does Rivetina archibaldi eat?
items.answer: Rivetina archibaldi is a ground-dwelling ambush predator. Its body plan supports a diet of small ground-active arthropods such as ants, beetles, and spiders.

items.question: Is Rivetina archibaldi a game character?
items.answer: No. Rivetina archibaldi is a species of praying mantis described in the scientific literature, not a game character or virtual pet.
